blocks.text: The Heights Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: The Official Community Plan (OCP) names it "Massey Victory Heights," residential neighbourhood 8 of 9 on the mainland; buyers shorten it to "The Heights."

It runs from East Tenth Avenue (the Burnaby border) south to East Eighth Avenue, east of McBride Boulevard — the line the City's Sapperton / Massey-Victory Heights Transportation Plan uses for this part of the city.
Neighbours: McBride Sapperton (OCP neighbourhood 9) east, Glenbrooke North west, Queen's Park south-west.

blocks.text: The Heights Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Houses sit in the OCP designation "(RD) Residential – Detached and Semi-Detached Housing": detached houses and duplexes, plus a secondary suite and a laneway or carriage house per lot.
Base zoning is the Single Detached Residential District (RS-1): single detached dwellings, secondary suites, and laneway or carriage houses.

Character is guarded: the City's heritage consultant confirmed the decorative street lights have heritage value — five originals on Churchill Avenue will be refurbished — and the neighbourhood has its own City Historic Neighbourhood Context Statement.
Curving Mott Crescent and Courtney Crescent anchor the west; York Street, Massey Street, William Street and Churchill Avenue run east.

blocks.text: The Heights Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The Province's small-scale multi-unit housing law needed no broad rezoning here: most house lots already allowed a house plus suite and laneway house. About 160 duplex lots were rezoned to RD-1 by Bylaw No. 8453, 2024, to add rental secondary suites.

The Queen's Park Heritage Conservation Area — the city's only one — does not cover The Heights, but a Heritage Alteration Permit can still apply to a house protected by its own designation, Heritage Revitalization Agreement or covenant; check the Heritage Protection Map.

blocks.text: The Heights Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Electricity is not BC Hydro: the City runs its own Electrical Utility, billing residential accounts every two months.
F.W. Howay Elementary sits inside the neighbourhood at 91 Courtney Crescent (district address list dated 2017).
təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre is at 65 East Sixth Avenue, just south; Royal Columbian Hospital is at 330 East Columbia Street in Sapperton.
The old lighting is a direct-buried system below current electrical standards, so the City says faults are hard to locate and repairs slow until replacement.

blocks.text: The Heights Houses: development and new projects

items.t: Massey Victory Heights Street Lighting Replacement (City of New Westminster, neighbourhood-wide): design complete, contractor retained, construction expected late May 2026, Zone 1 then Zone 2, five Churchill Avenue poles refurbished. Status: proceeding; Council added preservation scope June 23, 2025; page updated May 19, 2026 (as of November 3, 2026).
Status: adopted (as of November 3, 2026).
Brunette Interchange, Highway 1: the City's transportation plan lists a future reconfiguration or replacement (plan dated June 2018).

blocks.text: The Heights Houses: costs and taxes

items.t: Total 2026 residential (Class 1) property tax rate: $4.79312 per $1,000 of assessed value, per the City's 2026 mill rate schedule.

Utilities are a separate annual flat-rate bill: a single family dwelling pays $2,753.73 net for 2026 after the 5% discount (water $881.20, sewer $1,364.21, solid waste $508.32); a suite raises it to $4,143.46 net. Mailed late February; discount needs payment by May 4, 2026.
2026 Home Owner Grant: up to $570 basic, $845 at 65-plus, threshold $2,075,000, claimed with the Province.

blocks.text: The Heights Houses: getting around

items.t: TransLink's 128 bus runs the south edge: "From 22nd Street Station via 7 Ave, 23 St, 8 Ave, Braid St, Rousseau, access road to Braid Station" (timetable effective June 8, 2026).
Sapperton and Braid station areas, east of the neighbourhood, are Frequent Transit Development Areas in the City's OCP Regional Context Statement (March 9, 2026).
Below Hume Park, the Brunette River corridor carries the Brunette Fraser Greenway trail that Development Permit Area 7.1 is designated in part to continue.

blocks.text: The Heights Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Lots near the Brunette River / Hume Park edge: check Development Permit Area 7.1 (Brunette River), whose guidelines lead with geotechnical hazard mitigation for steep bank slopes.
The Sapperton Reach, from Hume Park's east boundary to the Braid Station SkyTrain overpass, has a south-bank embankment steeper than 30 percent — a corridor-lot issue, not an interior-street one.
Heritage designation and Heritage Revitalization Agreements supersede Transit Oriented Development Area height and density entitlements — check the Heritage Protection Map before pricing a rebuild.

blocks.text: Jared's take on The Heights (Massey Victory Heights), New Westminster

Veterans-era crescents give The Heights its character as a New Westminster neighbourhood. Post-war houses and newer rebuilds line curving, tree-lined crescents, and the east-side slope looks over the rooftops to the Fraser River and Mount Baker.

The Heights home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

36 houses sold in The Heights with a median price of $1,420,000 (the middle half sold between $1,208,250 and $1,613,750), taking a median of 28 days to sell at 96.6% of the last list price; 8% sold above list. They had a median $580 per square foot, a median year built of 1954 and a median lot of 6,105 square feet.

faq.a: No. The figures are for detached houses only. Condos and townhomes are counted on their own page.
faq.q: Does this page include townhomes or duplexes in The Heights?

faq.a: Yes — that pairing is the pattern the City planned for. The Residential – Detached and Semi-Detached designation lets a principal unit include a secondary suite and a detached house add a laneway or carriage house, and RS-1 zoning allows all three on one lot.
faq.q: Can I have both a basement suite and a laneway house?

faq.a: No. New Westminster has exactly one Heritage Conservation Area, covering Queen's Park only, so Heights houses escape its Protected and Non-protected classes and design guidelines. A permit applies only where the individual property carries a designation, Heritage Revitalization Agreement or covenant.
faq.q: Is The Heights inside the Queen's Park Heritage Conservation Area?

faq.a: On the named streets, yes, in sequence. The City is replacing the end-of-life street lighting: conduit and bases first, old lights kept on until fixtures arrive, Zone 1 (Mott Crescent, Courtney Crescent) first, then Zone 2 (York Street, Massey Street, William Street, Churchill Avenue).
